cohort: The study included 2363 low-risk primiparous women in Poland who went into labor with the intention of giving birth vaginally.
finding: Women with continuous personal support during labor had lower odds of a c-section (OR = 0.12), while women given epidurals had increased odds of a c-section (OR = 3.55).
mod_finding: Continuous personal support during labor was associated with lower odds of a c-section, whereas epidural use was associated with increased odds of a c-section.
cross-section timing: During labor and at the time of birth
